name: Yujin Kim, Ph.D.
title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow
address: 2800 Plymouth Rd, NCRC B20-301W, Ann Arbor, MI 48109
tagline: I am an immune engineer designing nanobiomaterials that deliver biopharmaceuticals to immune cells and reprogram immune function to overcome refractory diseases.
bio:
I am a postdoctoral research fellow in the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor.

I received my Ph.D. in 2021 from the Department of Biological Sciences at KAIST, under the supervision of Prof. Sangyong Jon. During my doctoral training, I added materials design and engineering to a background in the life sciences, developing nanomaterial-based vaccines and immunotherapeutics.

Since joining Prof. James J. Moon's group at the University of Michigan in 2023, I have deepened the immunological reasoning behind the materials I design and developed the independence to lead my own line of research in in vivo immune cell engineering. Together, these two stages define how I work as an immune engineer at the interface of immunology, nanotechnology, and biomedical engineering.
